name: bigram_confusion_memory
hypothesis: Replacing the ASCII-only tokenizer with Chinese character bigrams will make similarity retrieval actually semantic, causing the confusion-matrix disambiguation phase to operate on meaningful signal rather than random noise, improving score above 27/100.

name: contrastive_correction_memory
hypothesis: Injecting a 'Mistakes to avoid' block of similar wrong→right correction pairs before the examples will steer the model away from fine-grained label boundary errors (e.g. 诈骗→合同诈骗, 行贿→单位行贿), improving score above 27/100 independently of confusion-matrix accumulation.

name: lesson_memo_memory
hypothesis: Calling the LLM once per error batch to synthesize compact generalizable rules (stored as 'lesson memos' and retrieved by bigram similarity at predict time) will improve over raw example retrieval by encoding patterns like 'use unit-form charges when the subject is a legal entity' that apply across unseen cases, pushing score above 39/100.

name: label_cluster_memory
hypothesis: Organizing retrieval by charge-label clusters (multi-charge targets split on ';', top-4 labels ranked by max-example similarity, one '### Charge: {label}' section per label with canonical header and explicit format instructions) will reduce suffix-format and wrong-sub-category errors compared to the flat similarity list, pushing score above 39/100.
